INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS

The power sector reforms in the state of Haryana were initiated by the Government of Haryana (GoH)
under the Haryana Reforms Act 1998 on 10th March 1998. The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission

generation of electricity, and Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited (HVPNL) to undertake transmission,
distribution and retail supply of electricity in the state of Haryana.

Subsequently in July 1999, two distribution companies viz. Uttar Haryana BijliVitran Nigam Ltd. (UHBVNL)
and Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. (DHBVNL) were separated from HVPNL to exclusively
undertake function of distribution and retail supply of electricity in their respective geographic areas.

CHS shall act as a single central system for all interactions with the consumers for their complaints and queries. It
shall have all possible modes for consumer interaction inbuilt into the system including on-call, web portal, SMS,
WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, chatbot, email etc.

Unified Omni-channel communication

i. Phone call through IVRS – IVRS solution, CTI and APIs for integration will be provided by Call center vendor of

DHBVN. Bidder shall be responsible for integrating with existing & future IVRS and CTI. Customers will be able
to directly register their complaints without any human intervention through computerized IVRS. The unique
complaint number will be immediately given to the caller by the IVRS, followed by confirmation through SMS/

 Get the bill information

shall define short codes for various services and consumer can send a defined messaged using short codes to
register complaints and get enquires. SMS and WhatsApp Gateway shall be provided by DHBVN. There
should be provision to broadcast predefined and prescheduled messages to consumers.

2.1.5.
Contextual analytics for complaints management

As the complaints related to power distribution have a context associated with them and without the context
analysis, lot of irrelevant complaints can be registered. For example, if there is an area shutdown due to
breakdown at the 33 or higher KV levels, a single fault will impact thousands of consumers and all complaints
should be combined to reduce duplication of the complaints. System shall intelligently identify such faults,
schedule the confirmation and shall allow combining of the complaints into a single complaint but still should
maintain individual ticket.

2.1.8.
Tripping/ Breakdown portal

A portal shall be developed to record all information regarding scheduled maintenance and shut downs at
the feeder or sub-station level so that consumer can be provided with appropriate information when they
call for outage related complaints. Primarily it shall be used by circle control room for entering the data.
The system shall also be integrated with RTDAS to capture feeder ON/ OFF status and generate alerts.
APIs for RTDAS integration shall be provided by DHBVN. Based on the level & area affected of
tripping/breakdown/fault the intimation shall also be given to the officers of DHBVN via
SMS/WhatsApp/Automatic outbound call.
In addition, the intimation shall also be broadcasted to pre-defined numbers of various RWAs, Public
Administration, Public representatives, eminent citizens etc. of that area. Regular update on the status of
breakdown/fault along with estimated time shall also be broadcasted.

The following testing steps are usually employed in the project lifecycle. The Lead Partner along with

Unit Testing - In unit testing, each piece of code has to be rigorously tested. At this stage testing
is done according to the priority of path of code. All the test results are logged in the defect
logging tools. After every the completion of testing, code is corrected for defect logs. This process
is iterative till criteria for successful testing is reached.
Integration Testing - Upon completion of unit testing, integration testing begins. The purpose is to
ensure distinct components of the application still work in accordance to customer requirements.
Test sets will be developed with the express purpose of exercising the interfaces between the
components. This activity is to be carried out by the Test Team. Integration test will be termed
complete when actual results and expected results are either in line or differences are
explainable/acceptable based on client input.
Incremental Integration Testing - Continuous testing of an application as new functionality is

added.
context: RFP for Customer Helpline and IT Facility Management Services > 2 SCOPE OF WORK > Test Execution

repository prior to the release of the software. The testing is done on priority basis of business
processes. All the defects are logged and assigned to respective component owners. The
component and unit testing is performed after the correction of code. However, it may depend on
size and type of individual test specifications. Impact analysis is useful to narrow done testing
efforts by identifying critical test cases affected due to code change.

Acceptance Testing – During the test scenarios definition, for each of the business scenario, an
acceptance criterion is defined. Acceptance criteria include expected behavior of the s/w
component and the expected results (data). Expected results form a part of the Exit Criteria. In
addition to expected result and behaviors, some conditions are also specified in the exit criteria.
